newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares open down, catch breath after record.
newsitem.headline: German shares open down, catch breath after record.

text.p: German shares opened floor trade on Wednesday lower, slowed down after Tuesday's race to new closing highs by both lower bond prices and a slightly weaker dollar.
The blue-chip 30 share DAX index traded down 0.37 percent at 3,555.11 points which was down 13.17 points from Tuesday's close but still slightly higher than the morning's pre-bourse IBIS DAX levels.
Dealers said that while Wall Street's 0.15 percent gain on Tuesday underpinned the index, softer bond prices and the dollar's level at 1.7215 marks was sapping some energy.
The market was also catching its breath before Thursday's Ascension Day holiday, when German markets will be closed. Trading will resume on Friday.

Among individual shares, German airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG came in with news of a 20 million mark profit in the first quarter of 1997 prompting an upbeat outlook for the entire year. Shares climbed 3.46 percent to 26.90 marks .

Shares in drugs and chemicals group Bayer AG fell 2.75 percent to 67.25 marks on news a final settlement would soon be reached -- forcing Bayer to pay some 460 million marks to friends and relatives of more than than 6,000 hemophiliacs infected with Aids through tainted blood products.
